Found 2026-11-17 while fixing pm-ycgb5g. The credential_key_assignment value grammar (CREDENTIAL_VALUE in src/core/shared/secret-rules.ts) still excludes every value whose first characters are a reference or placeholder ($, <, ${, $(), so a literal concatenated with a reference is never judged: api_key=${EMPTY}"<credential>", api_key=$VAR"<credential>", "client_secret": "${EMPTY}<credential>", token: <x><credential> and the literal default api_key=${KEY:-<credential>} all pass the SDK guard (measured with scanMutationSecrets on the 2026-11-16 build; api_key=<credential>${VAR} is already detected). pm-ycgb5g fixed the same hole for password_assignment with a whole-value rule: the value is captured whole and minimumLiteralLength judges literalAfterReferences, the literal left once references expand to nothing. The two key-named rules now also disagree on a bare $VAR reference: [sample: a password assignment to a bare shell variable] is still reported by password_assignment, while api_key=$API_KEY is allowed by credential_key_assignment. Fix direction: give credential_key_assignment the same whole-value reference judgment (entropy measured on the literal after references expand), and decide one bare-$VAR policy for both rules with a must-allow entry for shell variables. credential_key_assignment is mutation-only, so the false-positive check is the pm-1l85at corpus rather than the repository scan. Duplicate check: searched credential_key_assignment reference placeholder concatenated literal; pm-ycgb5g (password rule only) and pm-jcz7qz (adversarial corpus) are related, and neither owns the credential-key reference grammar.

value.text: Design (implementation on branch fix/secret-guard-reference-literals-and-property-names). credential_key_assignment now captures a value whole when it holds a run-time reference (braced, command, dollar-name or angle placeholder) or opens with a quoted piece concatenated to more text, and judges the literal left once references expand with CREDENTIAL_LITERAL_VALUE: the unchanged reference-free grammar (paths, URLs, words, member paths, key-file names excluded; 8+ characters; entropy 3) read as one double-quoted literal, because the literal is data. The rule gains minimumLiteralLength 8 and a new declarative SecretRule field literalValue; acceptsSecretMatch judges the literal (not the captured text) for entropy and rejectValue whenever a rule declares a literal minimum. judgedLiteral treats a capture whose quotes the grammar read outside it (a quoted credential-key body) as data, so its quote characters are literal. Bounds: at most 64 literal characters before the first reference (a longer prefix is judged as a reference-free value), references and quoted pieces are whitespace-free (so a spaced command substitution is never one value and a key inside it keeps its own verdict), every repeated group is bounded at 4096 and quoted pieces at 4, as in the password grammar. Bare dollar-name policy (one policy for both key-named rules): a dollar-name reference expands to nothing when the name is CONSTANT_CASE (environment-variable convention) or when it is the whole value, quoted or not; bareness is judged on the source text, so a concatenation never reads as one name. Any other dollar text is literal, so a credential that merely contains a dollar sign keeps its characters.

value.text: Codex review round 1 on PR 1746 (gpt-6.1-sol, xhigh) found two credential-key regressions against main, both fixed. First: a quoted credential followed by member access was read as a concatenation, and the literal then looked like a dotted member path. Concatenation now opens only when the quoted piece holds a reference, or a reference or another quoted piece follows it directly, so reference-free code keeps its quoted-value reading. Second: a key inside a rejected referenced value, after a variable-led path, inside an angle placeholder, or two references deep, was hidden from the flat scan. The rule now declares a baseline reading (new SecretRule.baseline: its own flat pattern and structured value grammar), and the unchanged reference-free grammar is scanned too in text, structured, element and payload-member spellings. A value is reported when either reading reports it, so the referenced reading only adds findings and every key the reference-free scan visits keeps its verdict. Regression rows were added for all five shapes, plus one keeping a quoted prefix concatenated with code clean.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 2 on PR 1746 found that the first dollar-name policy (every CONSTANT_CASE name expands to nothing) dropped a credential that contains a dollar sign followed by an uppercase run after other characters, including an escaped dollar in a quoted value, which main reports. The policy is narrowed to the smallest change from main: a CONSTANT_CASE dollar-name expands to nothing only when no literal text precedes it in its word (the value or a default word), and a bare dollar-name of any case (the whole value) still spells nothing. Any other dollar text is literal. This supersedes the policy sentence in the close resolution. Rows were added for a CONSTANT_CASE name after literal text, an escaped dollar in a quoted value, and the payload-member spelling. The tracker false-positive scan is still 8 and 4 hits.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 3 on PR 1746 found two more regressions against main, both fixed. First, the baseline reading was judged with the new reference-expanding predicates, so a quoted value whose command substitution holds an assignment spelled two characters and was dropped. The baseline is now judged exactly as main judged it: on the captured text, with the value and entropy predicates but no literal minimum or literal grammar. Credential-key findings are therefore structurally a superset of main's. Second, a bare or leading dollar-name was decided on a capture that the password grammar had cut short at a colon, slash or question mark, so a password variable followed by a literal suffix was dropped. A dollar-name now counts as a reference only when the value grammar read the whole word, that is, when the match ends the input or a word-ending character follows it; otherwise its text stays literal, as on main. Rows were added for both shapes. Timing fixtures were also halved after an instrumented run on a host at load 15 to 20 came close to the 5-second bound.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 4 on PR 1746 found a missed literal and a new false positive, both fixed. (1) Word completeness trusted a following bracket, brace or comma as the end of a shell word, so a password variable followed by a bracket and a literal suffix was dropped. A word now counts as read whole only when nothing but punctuation follows the match before whitespace or the end of the text. The look-ahead is bounded at 64 characters, so judging stays linear. (2) A quoted reference followed by a method call opened a concatenation, and the method name became the apparent credential. Concatenation after a quoted piece that holds a reference now needs a letter, digit or underscore next. A literal that is only a member chain left after a reference is treated as code. Rows were added for bracket, brace, comma and parenthesis suffixes, a JSON string holding a bare variable, and three code-after-reference shapes, all clean or flagged as main reports them.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 5 on PR 1746 found a new false positive, fixed. After the equals sign, the referenced reading read the shell control operators as value characters, so a command substitution followed directly by a double pipe and a fallback command spelled the fallback as a credential. The bar and ampersand now end a referenced value, because they end a shell word. The baseline reading still reads them in a reference-free value, as main does. Rows were added for a double pipe, a double ampersand and a pipe after a variable.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Review round on PR 1746 (Greptile four P1s on intermediate heads, Codex round 6 two P2s), all fixed. (1) A referenced credential inside a rejected referenced value was no longer judged once rescans were limited to the password rule. credential_key_assignment now rescans a rejected referenced value shallowly: each inner key is judged once with the referenced grammar and the scan resumes after it, so each character is read at most twice. The password rule keeps the deep rescan. (2) A punctuation-led literal after a quoted reference was dropped by the alphanumeric-only continuation; the continuation now also accepts the non-operator symbols _ ! @ # % ^ ~ -. (3) The member-chain exclusion applied to payload data and quoted values too; it now applies only to unquoted source text. (4) In compact JSON the word look-ahead ran into the next member, so a bare variable was flagged. A closed quoted value followed by structure (a comma, colon, bracket, brace or semicolon, then whitespace, a quote, more structure or the end) now ends its word. (5) The 64-character look-ahead matched code points but was bounded in code units, so astral characters could make a truncated slice read as the end of the input. It now finds the punctuation run and checks the input at that exact code-unit position. (6) Question marks and colons after a reference are code (optional chaining, nullish coalescing, ternary), so they now end a referenced value, as the bar and ampersand do. Rows were added for every shape, including both JSON member orders.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Greptile on e8226f18b raised two more P1s, both fixed; neither is a regression against main. (1) Ending referenced values at every ampersand cut YAML data such as a reference followed by a literal holding a single ampersand. Only the double ampersand, the double bar and the pipe now end a referenced value; a single ampersand is data. Each run alternative is one character, so runs still cannot be split. (2) After a closing quote, two structure characters were accepted without checking what followed, so a quoted variable followed by a bracket, a comma and a literal lost the literal. The structure run (bounded at 64) must now be followed by whitespace, a quote or the end. Rows were added for both shapes and for a JSON array member that stays clean. Local note: stopping a running static gate leaves .cache/build-lease behind; the lease is the directory, so after confirming that no producer or consumer is alive, the empty directory must be removed, not only owner.json.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 8 on PR 1746 found two more boundary shifts against main, fixed by making the rules simpler, not wider. (1) Word completeness accepted any punctuation after a password variable, so a variable followed by a slash-and-plus suffix lost the suffix main reports. A word now ends only at whitespace or the end of the text, optionally after its closing quote and a bounded run of structure (semicolon, comma, closing parenthesis, brace or bracket). Any other text after the match is part of the same word. (2) The code exclusion required the whole literal to be a member chain, so member access on a reference followed by arithmetic became a finding. In unquoted source, a literal that starts with member access on a reference is now code.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Greptile on e4970e93a and Codex review round 9 on PR 1746 pulled the word-end rule in opposite directions: nested compact JSON with a bare variable was flagged, and an unquoted variable followed by an opening bracket, a brace or a comma and a quoted piece lost its literal suffix. The rule now separates the two cases. An unquoted value ends its word only at whitespace or the end of the text, optionally after structure. A quoted value, whose closing quote ends the capture or directly follows it, also ends its word when at least one structure character and then a quote, brace or bracket follow, as the next JSON member or element does. Two quoted pieces with nothing between them stay one shell word. Rows were added for every shape from both reviews.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 10 found a P1 regression against main: a quote after an unquoted password value was taken to close an enclosing string, but it can open a spaced concatenated piece, so a bare-looking variable followed by a quoted passphrase was dropped. A quote now counts as closing only when the grammar read the value as quoted: the capture ends with the closing quote, or its opening quote precedes the capture and the closing quote follows it. Otherwise the variable keeps main's literal reading. This deliberately gives back one earlier allowance: a bare variable directly before the closing quote of a string that holds a whole assignment is judged as on main. Greptile's member-access slip is fixed too: the exclusion now applies only when the capture starts with a reference, so a dotted literal that begins before the reference is judged. Both remaining CodeRabbit minors on e4970e93a are recorded on pm-jcz7qz rather than widened here, because main misses both shapes as well.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Greptile on fe8d8e598: the opening-brace-or-bracket allowance after structure also ended a shell word that continues with a bracket and literal text, so a quoted variable followed by a closing bracket, an opening bracket and a literal lost the literal that main reports. A brace or bracket now counts as the start of the next JSON element only when structure, a quote, whitespace or the end follows it. Rows were added for both bracket shapes and for a nested array element that stays clean. Codex review round 11 on c529018a9 found no actionable regressions.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Greptile on 40b325990: the stricter next-element check rejected a nested array that starts with a JSON number or literal, so compact JSON with a bare variable followed by such an array was flagged. After a brace or bracket the check now also accepts a JSON number, true, false or null followed by a non-word character, so a bracket followed by word text that merely starts with true still continues the shell word. Rows cover numbers, negative numbers, true, null, an empty object, both quote kinds, and the true-prefixed literal.

value.text: Codex review round 13 on PR 1746, two fixes. (1) A JSON number after a bracket was recognized from its first digit alone, so a bracket followed by a digit-led literal ended the shell word. A number, true, false or null now counts only as a complete token ended by a comma, closing bracket, closing brace or whitespace, within a 40-character look-ahead. (2) A TypeScript type assertion before a call left the function name as the literal after an angle placeholder. In unquoted source, a referenced value that a call's opening parenthesis follows is now code, like member access on a reference.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 14 on PR 1746, four fixes. (1) P1: after an unquoted key, a quoted variable followed by a comma and a quoted piece was taken for a JSON member; that is one shell word. The next-member shortcut now holds only when the value's own key is quoted, as in JSON, YAML flow or a Python dict. (2) A key inside a rejected command substitution, whose value ends at the substitution's closing parenthesis before the enclosing quote, kept its variable as literal text; a closing parenthesis or brace followed by a quote now ends an unquoted value's word. (3) The constant-statement exclusion tested the raw capture, so a type assertion before a constant was flagged; it now tests the derived literal (unchanged for the baseline reading). (4) Call detection now allows up to 16 blanks before the parenthesis.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 15 on PR 1746, two fixes. (1) The closing-parenthesis-or-brace word-end shortcut also applied at the top level, where such a character before a quoted literal is data, so a password variable followed by a brace and a quoted literal lost the literal. It now applies only to a match the rescan found inside a rejected reference value; those matches are tracked explicitly. (2) A type assertion before an optional call, a nullish fallback or a statement end left the identifier as a literal. A value led by an angle span is now code when such an expression continuation follows it.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 16 on PR 1746: the type-assertion findings kept arriving one operator at a time (call, optional call, nullish, logical fallback, index), so the family is now closed structurally. After an assignment's equals sign, a value led by an angle span is a TypeScript type assertion or generic, or a shell redirection, never a placeholder, so the referenced reading treats it as code. After a colon (YAML, prose) an angle placeholder before a literal is still judged, which keeps the acceptance example. The inner-match closing-delimiter shortcut now also covers a quoted inner variable inside a command substitution.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 17 on PR 1746: a binary operator after a reference in unquoted source was read as the start of a credential literal. The code-after-reference rules are now one rule. In unquoted source a value is code when an operator or member access follows its leading references, when a call's parenthesis follows it, or, after an equals sign, when an angle span leads it. A letter, digit or quoted piece after a reference is still a literal concatenation. This subsumes the member-access check. One policy row now spells the CONSTANT_CASE concatenation with a quoted piece, because a hyphen after a reference reads as subtraction.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 18 on PR 1746: a key inside a command substitution that another reference follows kept its variable as literal text, because the closing parenthesis only ended the inner word before a quote. For a match the rescan found inside a rejected reference value, the closing parenthesis or brace of that reference now ends the word whatever follows. At the top level such a character is still literal data.
